title: Conditional DETR for Fast Training Convergence
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)

problem.summary: DETR needs 500 training epochs because its decoder cross-attention relies heavily on content embeddings to localize the four box extremities: the spatial (positional) part of the attention contributes little, so short training leaves content queries too weak to match spatial keys and localization fails.
statements: DETR suffers from slow training convergence and needs 500 training epochs to reach good performance.

Cross-attention in DETR relies highly on content embeddings for localizing the four extremities and predicting the box, raising the need for high-quality content embeddings and thus the training difficulty.
Object queries only give a general attention weight map without exploiting the specific image information of the image.
Due to short training the content queries are not strong enough to match the spatial keys well, since they are also used to match the content keys.
Global encoder self-attention also causes high computation complexity in DETR.

evidence.quote: The DETR approach suffers from slow convergence on training, and needs 500 training epochs to get good performance.

the cross-attention in DETR relies highly on the content embeddings for localizing the four extremities and predicting the box, which increases the need for high-quality content embeddings and thus the training difficulty.
the spatial queries, i.e., object queries, only give the general attention weight map without exploiting the specific image information
This increases the dependence on high-quality content embeddings, thus increasing the training difficulty.

background.summary: The paper builds on DETR (end-to-end set prediction without NMS/anchors), on work addressing DETR's weaknesses such as deformable DETR, TSP and the concurrent SMCA, and on conditional/dynamic convolution ideas; the gap claimed is that prior fixes either change the attention structure or use human-crafted Gaussian attenuation, while none separates content and spatial queries to shrink the localization range.

relatedWork.name: DETR
relatedWork.quote: It effectively eliminates the need for many hand-crafted components, including non-maximum suppression and anchor generation.

relatedWork.name: Deformable DETR
relatedWork.relation: addresses DETR with sparse deformable attention and a high-resolution encoder instead of a new cross-attention
relatedWork.quote: handles this issue by replacing the global dense attention (self-attention and cross-attention) with deformable attention that attends to a small set of key sampling points

relatedWork.name: TSP
relatedWork.relation: alternative fast-convergence route that removes cross-attention and uses FCOS/R-CNN heads
relatedWork.quote: The TSP (transformer-based set prediction) approach [37] eliminates the cross-attention modules and combines the FCOS and R-CNN-like detection heads.

relatedWork.name: SMCA
relatedWork.relation: concurrent work modulating cross-attention with hand-crafted Gaussian maps
relatedWork.quote: It modulates the DETR multi-head global cross-attentions with Gaussian maps around a few (shifted) centers that are learned from the decoder embeddings, to focus more on a few regions inside the estimated box.

relatedWork.name: Anchor-based and anchor-free detectors
relatedWork.relation: mainstream alternatives that rely on initial guesses (anchors or object centers)
relatedWork.quote: Most existing object detection approaches make predictions from initial guesses that are carefully designed.

evidence.quote: DETR and its variants. DETR successfully applies transformers to object detection, effectively removing the need for many hand-designed components like non-maximum suppression or initial guess generation.
The other critical issue, slow training convergence, has been attracting a lot of recent research attention.

solution.summary: Conditional DETR replaces DETR's added query/key formation with concatenation of content and spatial parts and predicts a conditional spatial query from the previous decoder embedding and a learnable or predicted reference point, so each cross-attention head focuses on a band covering one extremity or an interior region and training converges much faster.
solution.approach: Predict a conditional spatial query from the decoder embedding and reference point, and form cross-attention from concatenated content and spatial queries/keys so localization range is narrowed per head.
components: conditional spatial query predicted from decoder embedding f and reference point s via an FFN and diagonal projection applied to the sinusoidal embedding of s
query/key formed by concatenating content and spatial parts instead of adding them, giving attention weight c_q^T c_k + p_q^T p_k
reference point either learned per prediction or predicted from the object query by an FFN
standard 8-head cross-attention with spatial and content parts projected separately per head
same DETR architecture otherwise: CNN backbone, transformer encoder, 6 decoder layers, shared prediction FFNs, 300 object queries
focal loss classification and L1+GIoU box regression following deformable DETR, with Hungarian bipartite matching

evidence.quote: Our approach, named conditional DETR, learns a conditional spatial query from the decoder embedding for decoder multi-head cross-attention.
each cross-attention head is able to attend to a band containing a distinct region, e.g., one object extremity or a region inside the object box.
our mechanism separates the roles of content and spatial queries so that spatial and content queries focus on the spatial and content attention weights, respectively.
The conditional spatial query is computed by transforming the reference point in the embedding space
We choose the simple and computationally-efficient projection matrix, a diagonal matrix.
The multi-head mechanism is beneficial to disentangle the localization tasks.

experiments.summary: Experiments use COCO 2017 with the DETR training protocol across four backbones (R50, R101 and their DC5 variants), comparing DETR and conditional DETR at 50/75/108 epochs against DETR at 500 epochs and against deformable DETR, UP-DETR, TSP and Faster R-CNN-FPN, plus ablations of reference points, conditional spatial query variants and projection forms.

evidence.quote: conditional DETR converges 6.7× faster for the backbones R50 and R101 and 10× faster for stronger backbones DC5-R50 and DC5-R101.
conditional DETR for high-resolution backbones DC5-R50 and DC5-R101 is 10× faster than the original DETR, and for low-resolution backbones R50 and R101 6.67× faster.
Our results over R50 and DC5-R50 are better than deformable DETR-SS: 40.9 vs. 39.4 and 43.8 vs. 41.5.
The comparisons in Table 2 surprisingly show that our approach on DC5-R50 (16×) performs same as deformable DETR-R50 (multi-scale, 8×).
Conditional crossattention in our approach built on the basis of focal loss and offset regression brings a major gain 4.0.

limitations.summary: The paper has no limitations section; stated constraints are that it targets training convergence only and leaves the encoder's high computation complexity unaddressed, it is not expected to match multi-scale or higher-resolution DETR variants, and at 50 epochs on R50/R101 it is still slightly below DETR trained for 500 epochs.
items: Global encoder self-attention complexity is not addressed; the method keeps the original DETR encoder.
Performance does not reach multi-scale or 8x-resolution DETR variants such as TSP-FCOS, TSP-RCNN and deformable DETR.
With only 50 epochs on low-resolution backbones R50/R101, accuracy is still slightly worse than DETR at 500 epochs.
Conditional DETR adds parameters and FLOPs over DETR (44M/90 GFLOPs vs 41M/86 GFLOPs for R50).

evidence.quote: We focus on accelerating the DETR training, without addressing the issue of high computational complexity in the encoder.
We do not expect that our approach achieves on par with DETR variants w/ multi-scale attention and 8×-resolution encoders
Conditional DETR with 50 training epochs for R50 and R101 as the backbones performs slightly worse than DETR with 500 training epochs.
